nodes.title: OpenAI
nodes.summary: Founded by Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever, Greg Brockman and others as a nonprofit AI lab; pivoted to 'capped-profit' in 2019 with major Microsoft backing.

nodes.title: Google DeepMind
nodes.summary: Formed by merging Google Brain (the home of the Transformer) and DeepMind into one AI unit to accelerate Google's response to ChatGPT.

nodes.title: Anthropic
nodes.summary: Founded by ex-OpenAI researchers Dario and Daniela Amodei; safety-focused lab behind Claude.

nodes.title: Meta AI (FAIR)
nodes.summary: Meta's AI research arm; drove the open-weight movement with the LLaMA family.

nodes.title: Mistral AI
nodes.summary: Paris-based lab founded by ex-DeepMind/Meta researchers; Europe's open-weight champion.

nodes.title: xAI
nodes.summary: Elon Musk's AI company, builder of Grok, integrated with X (Twitter).

nodes.title: DeepSeek
nodes.summary: Chinese lab (spun out of hedge fund High-Flyer) that shocked the industry with frontier-level models trained at a fraction of the cost.

nodes.title: The Transformer architecture
nodes.summary: "Attention Is All You Need" (Vaswani et al., Google) introduced the self-attention Transformer, the foundation of every modern large language model.

nodes.title: GPT-1
nodes.summary: OpenAI's first Generative Pre-trained Transformer (117M params); proved unsupervised pre-training + fine-tuning.

nodes.title: BERT
nodes.summary: Google's bidirectional encoder; dominated NLP benchmarks and powered Search, establishing pre-trained Transformers as the paradigm.

nodes.title: GPT-2
nodes.summary: OpenAI's 1.5B-param model, initially withheld as 'too dangerous to release'. The first mainstream debate about LLM risk.

nodes.title: GPT-3
nodes.summary: 175B params; few-shot in-context learning made the API era possible and seeded the modern race.

nodes.title: ChatGPT launch
nodes.summary: OpenAI releases ChatGPT (GPT-3.5). Fastest product to 100M users; the 'iPhone moment' that ignited the public LLM race.

nodes.title: LLaMA
nodes.summary: Meta's first LLaMA; weights leaked online and kicked off the open-weight ecosystem (Alpaca, Vicuna, llama.cpp).

nodes.title: Google Bard + Bing Chat
nodes.summary: Google rushes out Bard while Microsoft launches GPT-4-powered Bing Chat. The search-engine front opens.

nodes.title: GPT-4
nodes.summary: OpenAI's multimodal flagship; large jump in reasoning and the benchmark to beat for over a year.

nodes.title: Claude (1)
nodes.summary: Anthropic's first public assistant, emphasizing Constitutional AI and safety.

nodes.title: Grok
nodes.summary: xAI's first model, launched on X with a deliberately irreverent persona.

nodes.title: Claude 2
nodes.summary: Anthropic's 100K-token context model; pushed long-context as a differentiator.

nodes.title: Llama 2
nodes.summary: Meta releases Llama 2 under a commercial-friendly open license. The open-weight inflection point.

nodes.title: Mistral 7B / Mixtral 8x7B
nodes.summary: Mistral's efficient open models; Mixtral's mixture-of-experts matched far larger models and mainstreamed MoE.

nodes.title: Gemini 1.0
nodes.summary: Google's natively multimodal model family (Ultra/Pro/Nano); Bard rebranded to Gemini.

nodes.title: Gemini 1.5 Pro
nodes.summary: Up to 1M-token context window, a step-change in long-context that pressured every rival.

nodes.title: Claude 3 (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku)
nodes.summary: Anthropic's three-tier family; Opus was widely seen as the first model to clearly rival/beat GPT-4.

nodes.title: Llama 3
nodes.summary: Meta's strongest open weights yet (8B/70B, later 405B). Closed the gap to frontier closed models.

nodes.title: GPT-4o
nodes.summary: OpenAI's natively multimodal 'omni' model with real-time voice. Refocused the race on latency and interaction.

nodes.title: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
nodes.summary: Beat GPT-4o on many benchmarks at lower cost; later versions introduced Computer Use, making agents a front.

nodes.title: OpenAI o1
nodes.summary: First mainstream 'reasoning' model that thinks before answering. Opened the test-time-compute / reasoning era.

nodes.title: Gemini 2.0 + Flash
nodes.summary: Google's agentic, fast multimodal generation; Flash made cheap high-quality inference a competitive weapon.

nodes.title: DeepSeek R1
nodes.summary: Open reasoning model rivaling o1 at a fraction of the training cost; triggered a market shock and a wave of open reasoning models.

nodes.title: Grok 3
nodes.summary: xAI's frontier model trained on the massive Colossus GPU cluster; vaulted xAI into the top tier.

nodes.title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet
nodes.summary: Anthropic's first hybrid reasoning model (instant + extended thinking in one), with Claude Code for agentic coding.

nodes.title: GPT-4.5
nodes.summary: OpenAI's largest pre-trained (non-reasoning) model, emphasizing knowledge and 'EQ' as scaling-by-pretraining neared limits.

nodes.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro
nodes.summary: Google's 'thinking' model topped reasoning and coding leaderboards. Google decisively back at the frontier.

nodes.title: Llama 4
nodes.summary: Meta's mixture-of-experts open models (Scout/Maverick) with very long context, defending the open-weight frontier.

nodes.title: Claude 4 (Opus & Sonnet)
nodes.summary: Anthropic's flagship, setting new bars on agentic coding (SWE-bench) and sustained autonomous task execution.

nodes.title: GPT-5
nodes.summary: OpenAI's unified system that automatically routes between fast and deep-reasoning modes, folding the reasoning era back into one product.
